1 What Counts as Pressure? The Pre-Delivery Framework

Cricket analytics often errs by defining pressure simply as "the last five overs". In reality, a team needing 85 off 12 balls with 9 wickets down is in the 19th over, but the contest is virtually dead (zero leverage). Conversely, 30/3 in over 5 creates immense pressure.

CLUTCH-X evaluates pressure strictly on the pre-delivery state across all 201,000 balls (IPL & T20I, 2022–2026), preventing outcome leakage:

2nd Innings (Chasing Context)

  • Required Run Rate Stress ({RRR}$): Scaled against contemporary par.
  • Wicket Depletion ({wkt}$): Exponential penalty as wickets fall.
  • Innings Urgency ({urgency}$): Accelerates as balls run out.
  • Win Prob. Leverage ($): \cdot WP \cdot (1 - WP)$ dampens blowouts.

1st Innings (Target Setting Context)

  • Phase Leverage ({phase}$): Death overs 16–20 carry maximum swing.
  • Collapse Deficit ({collapse}$): Excess wickets lost vs expected.
  • Par Deficit ({deficit}$): Lagging behind 8.50 RPO par score.
  • Knockout Stakes: .15 imes$ multiplier for playoff/final matches.

2 Top 10 Batters Under Pressure: Clutch Batting Index (CBI)

The Clutch Batting Index (CBI) weights: 30% Pressure SR, 20% Dot-Ball Avoidance, 15% Dismissal Avoidance, 15% Boundary Production, 10% Delta vs Baseline, and 10% Match Consistency. Applied with Empirical Bayes shrinkage (=60$ balls) to eliminate small-sample noise.
